title: Client-side trust policy
description: The CONSUMER's policy, not the registry's. It answers: whose keys do I accept, which permissions may a package hold, which licences may enter my tree, what conformance score is my floor, and how do I behave when a signal is MISSING. The last question is the important one -- every `*_missing` knob defaults to `refuse`, because marketplace-first FM-5 measured 118 units whose declared contract was silently WIDENED to a permissive default, and a trust policy that widens on absence is the same defect wearing a security hat.

registry_maintainer_keys.description: Only these keys may sign a registry index. minItems 1: an empty list would make every index unverifiable, which mkt would then have to either refuse (breaking everything) or ignore (verifying nothing).

grant_permissions.description: Per-publisher widening ON TOP of max_permissions. Present so a first-party package can hold a permission a third party cannot, without weakening the global ceiling.

max_permissions.description: The GLOBAL ceiling. A package permission is admissible iff some entry here (or in the publisher grant) SUBSUMES it: `fs:read:workspace/**` subsumes `fs:read:workspace/a.txt`; nothing subsumes `fs:read:*` except `fs:read:*` itself. Subsumption is one function (mkt.permissions.subsumes) so the rule cannot drift between the linter and the installer.

forbidden_permissions.description: Hard denials evaluated BEFORE any grant. A pattern here cannot be re-enabled by a publisher grant -- otherwise the ceiling is advisory.

max_advisory_severity.description: The WORST open advisory severity that may still install. `none` means any open advisory refuses.

signature.description: Not tunable. A build in which an unsigned package can install is a build with no supply-chain control at all, so the schema itself refuses to express it.

allow_vulnerable_override.description: Whether an operator may pass --allow-vulnerable at all. Recorded in the install receipt when used, so an override is auditable rather than invisible.
